title: Flat localization in the second derived tensor factor
statement: Let $R\to A$ and $R\to B$ be maps of commutative rings, let $S\subset B$ be multiplicative, set $C=S^{-1}B$, and assume $B\to C$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $M$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For every $i$, the canonical map $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_B C\to H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C)$ is an isomorphism of $A\otimes_R C$-modules, natural in $M$ and compatible with the derived-category actions of $A$ and $B$. It is also compatible with the comparison maps: the square formed by $H^i$ of the canonical comparison map $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B\to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R B)$ tensored with $C$, $H^i$ of the comparison map $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C\to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R C)$, the above isomorphism, and the canonical map $H^i(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R B))\otimes_B C\to H^i(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R C))$ commutes.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) with flat base change of cohomology; equation comparison-map

proof.text: Let $I_S$ be the category with objects the elements $s\in S$ and, for $s,t\in S$, a morphism $t:s\to st$, composition being multiplication. It is filtered: $s$ and $s'$ both map to $ss'$, and if $t,t':s\to s'$ are parallel then $s(t-t')=0$, so the composites of $t,t'$ with $s:s'\to s's$ agree. Let $N_s=B$ for every $s$, with $t:s\to st$ acting as multiplication by $t$ (an $R$-linear chain map of complexes concentrated in degree $0$); the maps $\iota_s:B\to C$, $b\mapsto b/s$, are compatible and identify $C=S^{-1}B$ with $\varinjlim_{I_S}N_s$ (every element of $C$ is some $b/s$, and $b/s=0$ iff $ub=0$ for some $u\in S$, i.e. $b$ dies at the stage $us$). By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-derived-tensor] the maps $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\iota_s)$ induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_{I_S}H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\to H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C)$ of $A$-modules, natural in $M$, where the transition map for $t:s\to st$ is $H^i$ of the endomorphism of $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B$ induced by multiplication by $t$ on $B$, i.e. the action of $t\in B$ [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model], whose models are those of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (2).

source.place: Tags 06YR and 06Y6, filtered-colimit model for the localized second factor

proof.text: Put $H=H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)$, a $B$-module via the action of Step 1, and $\varphi=H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\iota_1):H\to H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C)$, the map induced by $B\to C$. The colimit over $I_S$ of copies of $H$ with transition maps multiplication by $t$ is $S^{-1}H=H\otimes_B C$, the element $x$ at stage $s$ going to $x\otimes(1/s)$ (the same elementwise verification as in Step 1). Since $\iota_s=\mu_{1/s}\circ\iota_1$ with $\mu_{1/s}$ multiplication by $1/s$ on $C$, functoriality gives $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\iota_s)(x)=(1/s)\cdot\varphi(x)$ for the $C$-action of [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model]; hence the isomorphism of Step 1 is the canonical map $H\otimes_B C\to H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C)$, $x\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot\varphi(x)$, which is therefore bijective. It is $C$-linear by construction and $A$-linear (hence $A\otimes_R C$-linear) and natural in $M$ by the naturality in $M$ of Step 1, the $A$-action being induced by the endomorphisms of $M$ given by multiplication by $a\in A$. Flatness of $B\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] holds for every localization and is not otherwise used.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, localization colimit and flat base-change cohomology

proof.text: Write $c_{R'}:M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R R')$ for the comparison map, $R'=B,C$. By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-action-naturality], for a K-flat resolution $P\to M$ over $A$ and $F\to R'$ over $R$, $c_{R'}$ is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R F)\to\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R R')=P\otimes_A(A\otimes_R R')$ induced by $F\to R'$, and $H^i(c_{R'})$ is $A\otimes_R R'$-linear. This is the value at $R'$ of the canonical transformation from the left derived functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P$ of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (2) to the functor $E\mapsto\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R P)$ on complexes of $R$-modules (a left derived functor comes with this transformation, and clause (2) says it is computed on K-flat resolutions), so it is natural with respect to the chain map $B\to C$: $H^i(c_C)\circ\varphi=\psi\circ H^i(c_B)$, where $\psi:H^i(P\otimes_R B)\to H^i(P\otimes_R C)$ is induced by $B\to C$, i.e. by $A\otimes_R B\to A\otimes_R C$. In the square of the statement all four maps are $C$-linear (the two maps out of a $-\otimes_B C$ by construction, $H^i(c_C)$ by the cited linearity, the isomorphism by Step 2), and $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_B C$ is generated over $C$ by the elements $x\otimes1$, on which the two composites are $H^i(c_C)(\varphi(x))$ and $\psi(H^i(c_B)(x))$; so the square commutes.
